label: Health
info:
Liveness probe for the gateway.

Deliberately shallow: it answers 200 whenever Node-RED is running the flow, and says nothing about AtroCore, Alfresco, Solr or the broker. That is a liveness check, not readiness, and the distinction matters here -- FOOTPRINT_AUDIT.md measured that a dead ActiveMQ makes some gateway calls hang indefinitely with no error, and a dead Solr makes others hang. A probe that reached upstreams would inherit those hangs and turn a health check into another way to wedge.

Checking upstreams belongs in Prometheus, which can time out and alert independently, not in the liveness probe a container restart policy depends on.

Implemented with a change node, not a function node, on purpose. A function node can throw -- the first version of this called process.uptime(), which the Node-RED sandbox does not expose, and the result was that the endpoint accepted the request and never answered. A liveness probe that hangs is worse than no probe: a hang is the one failure shape this platform already suffers from elsewhere (see FOOTPRINT_AUDIT.md on ActiveMQ) and the hardest to diagnose.

rules.to: {"status":"ok","service":"compliance_flow","checked":"gateway process only; upstreams are not probed"}
